predecessors.name: Western Chalukya Empire
predecessors.text: Telangana, held by Chalukya subordinates until the Kakatiyas 'assumed sovereignty ... in 1163 CE'

successors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
successors.text: the whole kingdom, annexed to the Delhi Sultanate on the fall of Warangal in November 1323

successors.name: Musunuri Nayaks
successors.text: the Musunuri Nayakas recovered Warangal from the Delhi Sultanate, dated 'as early as 1330' (Kakatiya dynasty page)

ledger.x: 1163: the Kakatiyas, under Rudradeva, end their feudatory status and rule Telangana from Anumakonda (Hanamkonda).
1195: the capital moves from Anumakonda (Hanamkonda) to Orugallu (Warangal).
1198: Yadava (Seuna) armies fight the Kakatiyas on the Telangana frontier.
1199: Mahadeva dies and Ganapati Deva ('r. c.
1201: the Kakatiyas hold the Krishna delta and Vela-nadu.
1208: Ganapati installs Tikka at Nellore.
1212: Kakatiya campaigns reach Kalinga.
1217: the Eastern Ganga king expels the Kakatiyas from Kalinga.
1217: Kalinga is lost.
1231: the Kakatiyas conquer Kolanu in Vengi.
1239: the Kadapa country comes under Kakatiya rule.
1263: Manuma-siddhi II, the Telugu Choda ruler of Nellore, is killed at Muttukuru and the line ends: 'The Pandyas captured Nellore, and killed Manuma-siddhi II in the Battle of Muttukuru in 1263 CE.'
1263: the Pandyas take Nellore.
1271: Naga-deva rules Nellore under Rudrama.

c. 1274: the Eastern Ganga prince Bhanudeva I invades Vengi. Narasimha I's son Bhanudeva I 'invaded Vengi around 1274 CE'; Rudrama's generals Poti and Proli Nayaka 'repulsed the Gajapatis, restoring Kakatiya control of coastal Andhra south of the Godavari.' The page names the invader as a Gajapati; the…
The invasion is repulsed.
1275: Naga-deva's rule at Nellore ends.
before 1281: Ambadeva's Kayastha principality breaks away with the Kadapa country and the Tripurantakam area.
1290: the Kakatiyas retake Nellore.
1291: Prataparudra's army marches on Ambadeva.
mid-1291: the Kakatiyas take Tripurantakam.
1294: Gona Vithala takes Raichur.

c. 1294: about 50 cells of Cliopatria's 1260 Kakatiya additions are in no Yadava shape of the yadava-dynasty dossier and in no event of this one; the Prataparudra II page gives only the 1294 Raichur Fort inscription and the Ramachandra page 'after 1296' for the Yadava land. Who held these cells before is on no page…
1309: Prataparudra ends the Kayastha rule.
1309: Mulikinadu is annexed.
January 1310: Malik Kafur besieges Orugallu.
February 1310: Prataparudra submits.

c. 1317: Kakatiya forces occupy Kanchi. 'After Alauddin's death in 1316, the Hoysala king Ballala launched a fresh invasion' of Pandya territory; the Kakatiya commander Peda Rudra defeated Ballala, and the Kakatiyas then occupied Kanchi; Devarinayaka's 1317 grant came after he defeated Vira Pandya and reinstated…
1318: Khusrau Khan marches on Warangal.
1318: Prataparudra submits again.
1323: the Kanchi occupation ends with the kingdom.
1323: Ulugh Khan (Jauna Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughluq) returns to Orugallu after the failure of 1321 and besieges it for five months.
9 November 1323: the siege of Warangal ends and Prataparudra is 'forced into submission'.
1323: the Kakatiya kingdom is annexed to the Delhi Sultanate.
9 November 1323: the Kakatiya dynasty ends with the fall of Warangal.

wars.name: Yadava invasion of the Kakatiya country
wars.outcome: Mahadeva died fighting the Seunas in 1198-1199 and Ganapati Deva succeeded; no land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of Vela-nadu and the Krishna delta
wars.outcome: The Kakatiyas held the region by 1201 and had annexed Vela-nadu and Karmma-rashtra by 1209.

wars.name: Kakatiya campaigns in Kalinga
wars.outcome: Ananga Bhima III expelled the Kakatiya forces from Kalinga sometime before 1217; Kakatiya control stayed south of the Godavari.

wars.name: Kakatiya raid on Kanchi
wars.outcome: The 1228 Mattevada inscription says Ganapati 'plundered the Chola capital', probably Kanchi; no land was taken.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of Kolanu
wars.outcome: The Iragavaram inscription of 1231 confirms the Kakatiya conquest of Kolanu in Vengi that year.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Nellore
wars.outcome: Around 1257 Jatavarman Sundara I subdued the Chola king and Kanchi; the Pandyas captured Nellore and killed Manuma-siddhi II at Muttukuru in 1263.

wars.name: Eastern Ganga and Gajapati invasion of Vengi
wars.outcome: Bhanudeva I invaded Vengi around 1274 and was repulsed by Poti and Proli Nayaka, who restored Kakatiya control south of the Godavari.

wars.name: Ambadeva's Kayastha revolt
wars.outcome: Ambadeva, chief from 1272, set up an independent principality south of the Krishna (the Kadapa country and Tripurantakam), killed Rudrama in November 1289 (a theory on indirect evidence), lost Nellore to Prataparudra in 1290 and Tripurantakam in mid-1291, and…

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of the Raichur Doab
wars.outcome: Gona Vithala took forts in Bellary district, the Raichur Doab and the city of Raichur in 1294; the zone is Cliopatria's 1260 additions.

wars.name: Khalji invasions of Warangal
wars.outcome: The 1303 raid by Malik Chajju and Fakhruddin Jauna failed at Upparapalli; Malik Kafur's month-long siege ended in February 1310 with annual tribute; Khusrau Khan's 1318 expedition raised the tribute to 100 elephants and 12,000 horses.

wars.name: Tughluq conquest of the Kakatiya kingdom
wars.outcome: Jauna Khan was repulsed in 1321 and retreated to Devagiri; he returned in 1323, besieged Orugallu for five months and Prataparudra surrendered on 9 November 1323; the kingdom was annexed.

wars.name: Kakatiya intervention in the Pandya civil war
wars.outcome: Peda Rudra defeated the Hoysala king Ballala, defeated Vira Pandya and reinstated Sundara Pandya; the Kakatiyas occupied Kanchi but, per the page, gained no lasting benefit.

certainty.note: Kakatiya frontiers rest on inscription find-spots and claims (Anagondi to Kalyani at the peak); no treaty line is recorded.

The tribute settlements of 1310 and 1318 fix no boundary; the Siege of Warangal (1318) article names the five demanded districts (Badarkot, Kailas, Basudan, Elor, Kobar) and says only Badarkot was ceded, none in the gazetteer, so nothing…
